result.summary: This draft pull request serves as a proof-of-concept demonstration completely removing AssumeUTXO (both snapshot loading and background validation) from Bitcoin Core. It eliminates multi-chainstate management, simplifies block download and pruning pipelines to a single active chainstate, and removes dynamic validation cache resizing, removing over 5,700 lines of code across 82 files.
result.problem: AssumeUTXO introduces significant architectural complexity into validation, block storage, networking, wallets, and cache management to support concurrent historical and snapshot chainstates. The author notes that background validation creates an ambiguous trust model, ordinary IBD performance continues to improve, and real-world adoption of snapshot bootstrapping remains low relative to its maintenance overhead.
evidence: Author references Core Dev meeting discussions: 'this follows our in-person discussion at the October 2026 Core Dev meeting. My impression was that there was rough agreement about the ambiguity background validation introduces: we trust a snapshot enough to use it immediately, but describe that trust as temporary until the same node finishes checking history.'
Author cites low adoption in PR #35054 discussion: 'adoption isn't where we hoped it would be'
The demo nets a reduction of 5,123 lines of code (-5795/+672) across 82 files by collapsing validation to a single owned chainstate.

enables: Targeted PRs carving out pieces of the simplification (e.g., dropping background sync or removing cache resizing)

result.scope_notes: This PR is explicitly an unmergeable demo branch intended to showcase what full removal looks like and to serve as a reference for smaller, carved-out PRs.
result.card: This draft demo PR demonstrates the complete removal of AssumeUTXO (snapshot loading and background validation) and is not intended for merge. It addresses the architectural and maintenance complexity of supporting multiple chainstates across validation, block storage, caching, and P2P download. The author cites Core Dev discussions on background validation trust ambiguity, low adoption of AssumeUTXO, and ongoing improvements to ordinary IBD speeds. It is based on #36601 and serves as a reference to gauge interest in carving out isolated simplifications.

risk.why: A mistake in refactoring core chainstate management, block index counts, or pruning bounds could cause chain stalls, database corruption, or consensus desync.
